GraceTechnology.Language: Go for the API; Python 3.12 for workers and Telegram adapter; TypeScript for Web and MCP; SQL migrations for PostgreSQL.
GraceTechnology.Runtime: Docker Compose local topology with uv-managed Python components, Go API, PostgreSQL, MinIO-compatible object storage, CopperASR runtime, Telegram Bot API, Web, and MCP services.
GraceTechnology.Framework: Go HTTP/WebSocket services; Python worker and aiogram Telegram adapter; TypeScript Web and MCP clients; CopperASR HTTP integration.
GraceTechnology.TestingStack: uv run pytest; Go tests via go test; pnpm Web/MCP tests and typecheck; disposable PostgreSQL contract tests; deterministic fixture and compose smoke scripts.
GraceTechnology.Observability: Structured diagnostics, correlation identifiers, analysis-run events, channel-surface events, analysis-step progress evidence, queue-specific lease evidence, and compose health checks.

OperationalConstraints.Constraint: Prefer existing repository libraries, contracts, fixtures, and test helpers; do not add speculative dependencies.

Analysis-run steps currently move from queued to running with a lease owner and timestamps, but do not yet have lease expiry or per-attempt-token fencing; that known gap is tracked by Bead media-j1qu. Export and metadata jobs use their own owner/token/lease controls.
API owns product lifecycle and performs no provider network call for remote metadata enrichment.
Object bytes are streamed through managed storage; physical deletion is scheduled only after transactional references and pins permit it.
Legacy ASR runtime paths, switches, caches, dependencies, and fallback tests remain excluded from active surfaces.

ArchitectureShape.ControlPlane: Go API owns public contracts, channel-account scope, validation, lifecycle transitions, operation requests, diagnostics, artifact metadata, retention, and channel-surface recovery.
ArchitectureShape.ExecutionPlane: Python workers consume sealed selection facts and declared analysis_run_step_inputs through internal APIs; they never infer durable state from mutable collections.
ArchitectureShape.QueuePlane: PostgreSQL analysis_run_steps, export_jobs, and metadata_enrichment_jobs are independent durable queues. Analysis-run steps currently use claim-once state and owner timestamps; export and metadata jobs use expiring leases and per-attempt tokens.
ArchitectureShape.ObjectPlane: MinIO-compatible storage keeps media bodies, previews, generated artifacts, private execution evidence, and diagnostic bundles behind API access decisions.
ArchitectureShape.AdapterPlane: Telegram, Web, and MCP are thin clients over shared API-owned media, collection, selection, run, artifact, diagnostic, account, and surface state.

TargetComponents.Component: apps/api: Go HTTP/WebSocket control plane, storage orchestration, and channel-account-scoped product authority.
packages/contracts: OpenAPI and shared target schemas.
workers/common: shared worker transport, source, object-store, document, and runtime helpers.
workers/transcription plus external/copper-asr: ordered transcript assembly and dedicated ASR runtime boundary.
workers/agent-runner: report and deep-research execution from prepared text artifacts.
workers/media-export: YouTube export and uploaded-video audio conversion behind export_jobs.
workers/metadata-enrichment: provider metadata retrieval behind metadata_enrichment_jobs.
apps/web, apps/telegram-bot, and apps/mcp-server: user and tool adapters over the API.
infra/docker-compose.yml: local service topology and health dependencies.

PersistentModel.Tables: channel_accounts, operation_requests, stored_objects, media_assets, collections, collection_items, selection_snapshots, selection_snapshot_items, analysis_runs, analysis_run_steps, analysis_run_step_inputs, analysis_run_events, export_jobs, metadata_enrichment_jobs, export_deliveries, stored_object_pins, artifacts, artifact_subjects, diagnostics, channel_surfaces, channel_surface_subjects, channel_surface_events.
PersistentModel.Rule: Physical uploaded bytes are unique by channel_account_id, SHA-256, and size, while media_asset occurrences and collection memberships remain distinct.
Selections are storage-enforced immutable; workers consume frozen item facts and declared inputs, not mutable collection rows.
Artifact lineage, diagnostics, idempotency records, and channel-surface event history remain durable even when object bodies expire.

PublicApiSurface.Surface: Media create/upload/list/get/delete and scoped metadata refresh.
Collection inbox/list/create/update/item mutation and atomic processing launch.
Artifact preview/download refresh, diagnostics query, export create/list/read/cancel/retry/delivery/download, and WebSocket updates.

InternalApiSurface.Surface: Analysis step claim/cancel-check/progress/finalize, request-access, reusable transcript lookup, artifact and diagnostic registration.
Export and metadata queue/claim/progress/cancel/finalize/reclaim plus retention sweep/reconcile; all require platform-token protection.

LifecycleAndRetention.Rule: Soft-deleted product records remain hidden from default reads while immutable snapshots and run history survive object-body expiry.
MEDIA_OBJECT_RETENTION_DAYS defaults to seven; each storage generation expires from the later of publication and last successful use.
Pin insertion succeeds only while an object is available; delete scheduling proves no active pins under the same database fence and blocks new work before physical deletion.

Publication, source work, delivery, delete claims, exports, and metadata enrichment use their implemented owner/token/lease compare-and-set transitions with bounded retry; analysis-run-step lease expiry and attempt-token fencing remain pending under media-j1qu.
S3-compatible storage is durable byte authority; attempt workspaces stream in bounded chunks, clean in outer finally, and are reaped only after lease grace or absolute TTL.
Private-state host ports bind locally, hostile Host/Origin requests fail before handlers, internal routes require PLATFORM_INTERNAL_TOKEN, and public DTOs never reveal object keys.

AsrRuntime.Source: external/copper-asr is the pinned external runtime source; workers/common/src/transcriber_workers_common/copper_asr.py is the platform client boundary.
AsrRuntime.Contract: Platform owns inputs, lifecycle, progress, cancellation, artifacts, diagnostics, and channel surfaces; CopperASR owns model lifecycle, inference, sanitized ASR errors, health, and transcribe endpoints.
AsrRuntime.Topology: Dedicated internal copper-asr service is called through COPPER_ASR_BASE_URL and bounded CPU, ONNX, Torch, ffmpeg, cache, temporary storage, and health-start settings.
AsrRuntime.Policy: Local compose uses the CPU runtime profile unless a later approved change modifies the image and benchmark envelope.

AdapterContracts.Telegram: Capture inputs through local Telegram Bot API, resolve channel scope, manage API state, recover channel surfaces, and deliver API-resolved artifacts with fenced duplicate prevention and correct voice/audio/document presentation.
AdapterContracts.Web: Present materials, collections, selections, progress, results, downloads, errors, and retention without normal-surface service metadata.
AdapterContracts.Mcp: Expose stable tools over the API and allow explicit service-artifact previews without a separate durable media store.

EvidenceContracts.ContractEvidence: Prove target DTOs/routes, validation, canonical vocabulary, and removal of stale aliases.
EvidenceContracts.StorageEvidence: Prove migration/reset, identity, publication, pins/deletion, queues, immutable snapshots, idempotency, diagnostics, surfaces, lineage, and reconciliation on disposable PostgreSQL.
EvidenceContracts.WorkerEvidence: Prove queue claims, declared inputs, provider bounds, publication, cancellation, resource limits, scratch cleanup, diagnostics, and restart recovery.
EvidenceContracts.AdapterEvidence: Prove all adapters use shared API state, channel recovery and delivery are restart-safe, and normal presentation hides provider internals.
EvidenceContracts.RuntimeEvidence: Prove real ingestion, atomic launch, analysis, export/delivery, restart recovery, digest reuse, scratch cleanup, and physical object expiry through the compose topology.
